definition: Used to join words or ideas.
exampleSentence: My sister and her husband live in a small town.
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
First we had lunch, then we visited the old castle.
The bridge is closed, hence the long traffic jam this morning.
He did not study; consequently, he failed the exam.

definition: In a way that suits the situation.
exampleSentence: The rules have changed, so please update your plans accordingly.

definition: Because of what was just said.
exampleSentence: The road is icy; for this reason, the school will open late.

definition: Used to give the result of something just said.
exampleSentence: I missed the bus, and that is why I was late today.

definition: Used to add a fact, often a surprising one.
exampleSentence: As a matter of fact, I have already finished the report.

definition: Used to confirm or add emphasis.
exampleSentence: It was indeed the best concert I have ever seen.
I like all sports, but football in particular.
Two students, namely Ali and Ayşe, won the prize.
I enjoy outdoor activities such as hiking and cycling.

definition: Except for, or in addition to.
exampleSentence: Apart from the price, I really like this apartment.
Everyone came to the party except for my cousin Tom.
I prefer to walk to work rather than take the bus.

definition: In addition, usually to something bad.
exampleSentence: The train was late; on top of that, it started to rain.

definition: Used to add another important point.
exampleSentence: The laptop is light; what is more, the battery lasts all day.
Plants need water, and in the same way, people need sleep.

definition: Used to show a clear difference.
exampleSentence: The old phone was slow; by contrast, the new one is very fast.
The hotel was old; even so, we enjoyed our stay there.
All in all, it was a successful year for our company.
Overall, the customers were happy with our new service.

definition: Used to give a short version of what was said.
exampleSentence: In summary, we need to reduce costs and improve quality.

definition: At the start; first of all.
exampleSentence: To begin with, let me introduce myself and my team.

definition: Used to introduce the first point.
exampleSentence: Firstly, I would like to thank our sponsors for their support.

definition: Used to introduce the second point.
exampleSentence: Secondly, we need to hire two more developers this year.

definition: Used to introduce the final point.
exampleSentence: Lastly, please remember to sign the attendance sheet.
We watched a movie and went for dinner afterwards.
At last, the long winter was over and spring arrived.
I will call you as soon as I land in Madrid.

definition: Before or at the time when.
exampleSentence: By the time we arrived, the movie had already started.
You can borrow my car provided that you return it tonight.
She looked as though she had not slept for days.
Now that I have a car, I can visit my parents more often.
Given that it is raining, we should take a taxi.

definition: In the time between two events.
exampleSentence: The doctor will see you soon; in the meantime, please fill in this form.
We left early so as to avoid the traffic.
You are tired? In that case, let us stay home tonight.
We can take the bus or the train; either way, we will arrive by noon.
